text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- President Hosni Mubarak says the peace process is passing through the most difficult stage since 1977. Mubarak tells a news conference that what is going on in Jerusalem threatens all peace efforts. The president warns that building a settlement on Jabal Abu Ghneim (in Jerusalem)will be the beginning of a new era of violence.
- Mubarak received a telephone call from Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Wednesday evening. The two leaders discussed current contacts to contain the deterioration in the peace process.
- Mubarak to meet Palestinian President Yasser Arafat and Lebanese Prime Minister Rafik al-Hariri.
- Mubarak received a telephone call from Syrian President Hafez Assad. The two leaders exchanged views on the deteriorating situation in East Jerusalem.
- Egypt receives $58.3 million from the U.N. damages committee as a first payment for those who affected by the Gulf crisis in 1990 and 1991.
- At the opening of Cairo International Fair. Prime Minister Kamal Ganzouri says Egyptian products are developing steadily and will be capable of international competition.
